prompts.task: Run $otel-audit against the Python service in ./service. Do not modify service code, dependencies, configuration, tests, or organization policy. Only write and validate the canonical .observe audit artifacts.

judge_inputs: Inspect ./service source, startup files, manifests, OBSERVABILITY.md, and generated .observe artifacts.
Read ./last_message.md for the agent final response.
rubric: Identifies that Click itself does not choose trace lifetime: cli.py keeps click session current around several independently scheduled task process spans, so the source-defined boundary collapses them into one trace; requires one fresh root trace per task, with a span link rather than parentage when delayed upstream causality must be retained.

Inventories the exact Gunicorn preload, Uvicorn multi-worker, provider construction, background processor, worker class, and shutdown topology per signal. It flags provider creation in the preload master as partial or unsafe until worker-local runtime proof and does not claim that every multi-worker stack necessarily emits only one trace.

Treats Conda as an interpreter, environment, executable, and package-inventory boundary rather than an unsupported-library category. It identifies that conda-bad resolves opentelemetry-instrument outside customer-python and requires proof from the target environment for Python, agent, distro, and matching instrumentation packages.

Reads OBSERVABILITY.md as organization-owned constraints, validates it against source and launch evidence, preserves its service identities and privacy limits, and reports conflicts rather than allowing policy prose to override observed runtime facts or OpenTelemetry safety rules.

Creates a focused call-site scenario for Click task trace independence and separate full-runtime scenarios for Gunicorn worker-local provider ownership and all configured signals, Uvicorn multi-worker signal behavior, and Conda environment/launcher alignment.
